justification: Assessment reports INVALID at line 0045, targeting the same defect as ground truth: the proof's unproved (and false) claim that any non-conflicting color choice suffices, i.e. a non-conflicting color is always available. Ground truth witnesses this with the icosahedron; the assessment supplies a different but valid witness (a 25-vertex planar graph). I replayed the assessment's trace: Round 1 picks v1 (max degree), legally colors w1=1, w2=2, a_i=1, l_i=1; Round 2 is forced to v2 (ColoredDegree 5 > u's 2), legally colors w3=3, w4=4; Round 3 is forced to v3 (ColoredDegree 5 > u's 4), colors v3=2 and w5=5 (legal, w5's only colored neighbor is v3=2). Vertex u then has neighbors colored 1..5 and cannot be colored. Every B choice was non-conflicting when made, and the graph is planar (subdivision of a K4 subgraph plus parallels/pendants). Different-but-valid witness for the same flawed claim: CAUGHT_MATCHING.
